title: Video Player
description: A video player with overlay controls: play and pause, a scrubber with a hover preview, time, volume, Picture-in-Picture and fullscreen, with lazy loading and muted autoplay.

props.name: src
props.description: The video URL. It is set on the video only when the player nears the viewport (lazy loading).

props.name: aspectRatio
props.description: The player's CSS aspect ratio; the video covers it.

props.name: preloadMargin
props.description: Root margin of the lazy-load observer: how far ahead of the viewport the video starts loading.

props.name: autoPlay
props.description: Muted, looping autoplay once loaded (browsers allow muted autoplay). Skipped under prefers-reduced-motion.

props.name: controls
props.description: Adds the control tray: mute and volume, Picture-in-Picture and fullscreen. Without it the player shows play and pause and the scrubber only.

props.name: showTime
props.description: With controls, a pinned time button (click to switch elapsed and remaining); without, a time tooltip over the scrubber while hovering or dragging.

props.name: pauseOnOverlayClick
props.description: On desktop pointers, a click anywhere on the video surface plays or pauses.

props.name: volume / volumeSlider / pictureInPicture / fullscreen
props.description: Each control of the tray (needs controls). The mute button hides itself when the video has no audio track.

props.name: videoRef
props.description: The underlying video element, to play, pause or seek from outside.

props.name: children
props.description: <track> elements (captions, subtitles), passed through to the video.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The name of the player group; describe the video.

a11y: The player is a focusable group named by aria-label: Space, Enter and K play or pause it, and hardware media keys work through the Media Session API. The play button's name follows the state (Play video, Pause video).

The scrubber is a slider (WAI-ARIA slider pattern) with the time as aria-valuetext ("0:03 of 0:10"): Left and Right seek 5 s (10 s with Shift), Page Up and Page Down 10%, Home and End jump to the ends. The volume slider is vertical: Up and Down step 5% (10% with Shift), Home and End mute or max it; it opens while it has keyboard focus.

Every control is a native button with a name and a visible focus ring (the play button and the player itself gained one: upstream drew none). Focusing a control reveals the controls. The elapsed and remaining time button is focusable and named (upstream kept it out of the tab order).
Reduced motion: no autoplay, and the controls appear and hide without fades, slides or the loading shimmer.

Contrast on request: under prefers-contrast: more the glass behind the time and controls turns opaque dark; under forced colors the bars use Highlight on Canvas. The default keeps upstream's translucent glass over the video.
Captions: pass <track kind="captions"> children; the browser renders the default track over the video. Give cues a line setting (for example line:72%) to keep them above the scrubber and tray.
Right to left: the control tray and the pinned time swap sides and the tray's buttons mirror; the timeline and the play glyph stay left to right, as in native players.
docs:
Installed `VideoPlayer` in `components/ui/` (with its controller, stylesheet, helpers and icons next to it).

```tsx
import { VideoPlayer } from "@/components/ui/video-player";

<VideoPlayer src="/video.mp4" aria-label="Product tour" />
<VideoPlayer src="/video.mp4" controls showTime autoPlay={false} />
```

The video loads lazily and autoplays muted and looped (not under reduced motion). `controls` adds the mute, volume, Picture-in-Picture and fullscreen tray; `showTime` adds the time. Pass `<track>` children for captions (give cues a `line:72%` setting so they clear the scrubber) and `videoRef` to control playback.

The stylesheet is rendered by the component (a React 19 hoisted `<style>`); no CSS import is needed. Size it with `className` (it is `w-full` with an aspect ratio) and theme it with the `--video-player-*` variables (background, foreground, overlay, glass, focus ring). The `-icons-lucide` and `-icons-phosphor` items use icon-library glyphs instead of the player's own.

Ported from SimplePlayer by grizz (MIT); the license notice is at the end of every file.
